title: Begin with humanity
shortDescription: See people first. Protect dignity before argument, ideology, or action.
whyItMatters: Responsible action begins by keeping vulnerable people and human dignity at the center.
questionToAsk: Who is most vulnerable, and how do I keep their humanity central?
safetyNote: Do not use people’s suffering as content or proof of virtue.

title: Regulate yourself before responding
shortDescription: Notice fear, grief, anger, urgency, shame, and reactivity before acting.
whyItMatters: Unregulated urgency can lead to harmful claims, public shaming, or unsafe action.
questionToAsk: What is happening in me before I speak or act?
safetyNote: This is reflection, not therapy or medical advice.

title: Verify reality
shortDescription: Separate what is known, sourced, uncertain, and not ready to repeat.
whyItMatters: Accurate support depends on source discipline and humility about uncertainty.
questionToAsk: What do I know, and how do I know it?
safetyNote: No claim without a source and review status.

title: Understand the system
shortDescription: Look beyond one event. Notice patterns, actors, constraints, feedback loops, incentives, history, and future risk.
whyItMatters: System awareness helps people avoid shallow or harmful action.
questionToAsk: What system is producing this situation?
safetyNote: System analysis requires local validation and source review.

title: Read the level of complexity
shortDescription: Clear, complicated, complex, chaotic, and uncertain contexts require different behavior.
whyItMatters: The wrong response to the wrong context can increase harm.
questionToAsk: What kind of situation am I actually in?
safetyNote: Do not present uncertainty as certainty.

title: Listen across difference
shortDescription: Do not flatten people into categories. Listen for identity, fear, values, grief, dignity, and needs.
whyItMatters: Listening can reduce dehumanization without requiring agreement.
questionToAsk: What is this person or group protecting?
safetyNote: Do not force dialogue or disclosure of identity, grief, or trauma.

title: Communicate without dehumanization
shortDescription: Speak with moral clarity while preserving human dignity.
whyItMatters: Language shapes whether repair becomes more possible or less possible.
questionToAsk: Does my language make repair more possible or less possible?
safetyNote: No dehumanizing language, unsupported claims, or shame-based messaging.

title: Protect the vulnerable
shortDescription: Children, displaced people, traumatized communities, and crisis-affected people require safeguarding.
whyItMatters: Good intentions can expose vulnerable people to risk if safeguards are absent.
questionToAsk: Could my action expose someone vulnerable to risk?
safetyNote: No direct unsupervised contact with minors or vulnerable people.

title: Choose a responsible pathway
shortDescription: Donate, advocate, learn, organize, build, partner, or teach through verified and safe pathways.
whyItMatters: Action becomes useful when it is routed through evidence, review, and safeguards.
questionToAsk: What is the safest useful next step?
safetyNote: No donation processing or unsupported routing in this prototype.

title: Build capacity with others
shortDescription: Move from individual concern to team learning, workshops, campus labs, partner projects, or safe learning circles.
whyItMatters: Sustained capacity is often built relationally and collectively.
questionToAsk: Who can I learn with, build with, or support responsibly?
safetyNote: Community and cross-community work must be partner-mediated and safeguarding-reviewed.

title: Practice, simulate, reflect
shortDescription: Practice through scenarios, create an artifact, reflect, and improve before acting.
whyItMatters: Practice lowers the chance of reactive or unsafe public action.
questionToAsk: What should I practice before acting?
safetyNote: Simulations are educational tools, not professional advice.

title: Play the long game
shortDescription: Ask what today’s action contributes to in 30 days, 12 months, 5 years, 10 years, and 25 years.
whyItMatters: Responsible action should connect urgent care to durable recovery and civic capacity.
questionToAsk: What capacity does this action build over time?
safetyNote: Long-arc reflections are not predictions or verified impact claims.
